answer.rationale: A is the stronger early-development choice for a conventional orally available small molecule: it has substantially lower molecular weight (about 319 versus 491 Da), fewer rotatable bonds, and a higher overall drug-likeness profile while remaining within standard oral-property limits. Although A is quite lipophilic and has very low polar surface area—liabilities that would need follow-up for solubility, promiscuity, and hERG risk—B sits close to the upper molecular-weight boundary and is considerably larger and more complex, making optimization and oral exposure less forgiving at this early stage.
